figures.caption: Micropile Classification System Based on Type of Grouting
figures.description: Construction Type Classification Identifying grouting Types A to D and sub-types 1 to 3 when reading bond values or specifications. Grouting method is typically the most sensitive construction process for grout/ground bond capacity, which varies directly with it Type A: gravity head only; sand-cement mortar or neat cement grout; underreaming possible but not common Type B: neat grout under pressure as temporary casing is withdrawn, typically 0.5-1 MPa (72-145 psi), avoiding hydrofracture Type C: gravity grout, then after about 15-25 minutes one injection via sleeved pipe, no packer, at least 1 MPa (145 psi); France only (IGU) Type D: gravity (or pressurized) grout, then after hardening injections via sleeved pipe at 2-8 MPa (290-1,160 psi), packer for repeat horizons (IRS); used worldwide

figures.description: Overview Choosing a drilling method: hole stability, disturbance, flushing, timing and site constraints. Any method acceptable if it forms a stable hole of required size within tolerance without harming the surroundings Do not exclude a method because it does not fit a predetermined concept of the work Vigorous water flush can enlarge bond-zone diameter, but high flow and pressure risk voids, settlement and hydrofracture heave Drill, place reinforcement and grout each micropile continuously and expeditiously Overconsolidated clays and clay shales: complete the bond zone within one day (no hole open overnight) Scarce water, cleanliness, limited space or hazardous spoil may dictate air flush or augers

Statnamic: solid fuel in a pressure chamber accelerates a reaction mass upward, pushing the pile down; unloads by venting gas Load magnitude, duration and rate set by piston and cylinder size, fuel mass and type, reaction mass and venting Needs a level work area 3 to 4 m (10 to 13 ft) across and at least 8.5 m (28 ft) headroom (Figure 7-13) Advantages: no reaction system, quicker set-up, about one quarter to one half the cost of an equivalent static test Suits lateral tests, batter micropiles and over-water tests; no stress waves, so simpler analysis than dynamic tests Disadvantages: no creep test, no tension tests yet, may not suit tight access, needs expert interpretation
